acquisition.why: Inbound only: local SEO for exact-match terms, Google/Meta ads geo-targeted around visitor hubs, OTA listings (Viator/GetYourGuide). Agents can run these, but the business depends on platforms and Google.

onboarding.why: Booking widgets (FareHarbor/Bookeo) take bookings, waivers and confirmations unattended.

delivery.why: Physical tour or boat run by a guide or captain every time. Needs a licensed operator and insurance.

billing.why: Prepaid online booking. Refunds and weather cancellations need occasional human judgement.

support.why: Agents can handle FAQs. Weather, no-shows, group disputes and on-the-day issues need a human or the operator.

scores.R_why: Ricardo cannot guide tours himself, so the only workable version is a lead-gen site that passes bookings to existing UK operators (Thames boats, London film-location tours) for a commission. That fits 6-8 h/week and £300, but it relies on partner deals, is seasonal, and runs into Port of London Authority/MCA licensing and IP limits on film-location tours. The evidence is one US anecdote.
scores.M_why: London tours are saturated: Viator, GetYourGuide and established operators dominate search. Local niches outside London are thin and seasonal [E].
scores.one_line: Only the booking front-end can be automated. Delivery is physical, depends on a partner, and London is saturated, so it is a weak fit except as a small lead-gen site.

acquisition.why: Paid social, TikTok Shop and SEO are inbound, and agents can produce ad creative. Profitability depends on human-approved ad spend and platform algorithms.

delivery.why: White-label dropship or a 3PL handles fulfilment, but supplier QA and stock issues need human oversight.

support.why: Agents handle WISMO tickets and returns. Adverse skin reactions need a human.

scores.R_why: UK Cosmetics Regulation applies: each product needs a UK Responsible Person, a Cosmetic Product Safety Report and SCPN notification. That is costly and a heavy compliance load against a £300 budget. Brow serums with growth claims or peptide/medicinal claims risk ASA/MHRA action, and US dropship suppliers often aren't UK-compliant.
scores.M_why: Pimple patches and serums are hyper-saturated (Starface, Hero, Amazon and TikTok Shop clones). Ad costs are high and AI creative is commoditised [E].
scores.one_line: The storefront automates easily, but a saturated category and UK cosmetics compliance make it a poor £300 bet.

acquisition.why: Cold email to UK limited-company agencies is legal with an opt-out, and agents can research targets and draft spec demos. Personal Instagram/X DMs from the source should be dropped. Closing calls usually need Ricardo.

onboarding.why: Agents can run the brief intake form and asset collection. Brand-guideline nuance needs checks.

delivery.why: Veo/Sora/image pipelines generate the variants. A human curation and approval pass is needed because quality is inconsistent.

billing.why: Stripe invoices and retainers. Some agencies pay on net terms.

support.why: Agents can handle revision requests. Agency relationship issues need Ricardo occasionally.

scores.R_why: It is technical-friendly, needs about £100-200/month in tool credits, and UK agencies are reachable. Two weak risks: agencies demand responsiveness and revisions that clash with 6-8 h/week, and the claims are second-hand or hypothetical.
scores.M_why: Agencies are adopting Veo/Sora themselves, and creative tools such as Creatify and Arcads are commoditising ad variants fast. The window is shrinking in 2026 [E].
scores.one_line: A legal B2B cold-email path and an agent-heavy pipeline make this testable, but AI commoditisation and agencies bringing it in-house squeeze pricing.

acquisition.why: Organic social is inbound, but platform algorithms are fickle, and AI-faceless accounts get suppressed or demonetised.

onboarding.why: Signing up for affiliate and campaign programmes such as Higgsfield Earn and PartnerStack is self-serve.

delivery.why: Agents can script and generate content and schedule posts. Sponsored reads and quality need human approval, and talking-head formats need Ricardo on camera.

billing.why: Affiliate payouts are automatic. Direct sponsorship deals need negotiation.

support.why: Minimal support load, mostly comment moderation.

scores.R_why: The cost is low and it suits a technical person, but building an audience with real reach takes months of consistent output. The $1M+ claims are second-hand and survivor-biased. UK ASA/CMA #ad disclosure is mandatory, and UK eligibility for programmes like Higgsfield Earn is unclear.
scores.M_why: AI-tool creator content is flooded with automated accounts, sponsor budgets depend on AI funding cycles, and income is concentrated in a few platforms [E].
scores.one_line: Cheap to run and fairly automatable, but it is a long-shot audience game with hype-driven, second-hand income claims.

acquisition.why: Meta ads with AI creative, plus affiliate seeding to influencers (by email to creators' business addresses or through creator marketplaces). It is inbound and human-approved, but ad costs make or break it.

delivery.why: Heavy physical goods mean sourcing, stock, 3PL and expensive shipping of weights. Some human oversight is needed throughout.

support.why: Agents handle WISMO tickets. Returns of heavy items and damage claims need checks.

scores.R_why: An inventory MOQ from Alibaba plus UK import duty and VAT far exceeds £300. Shipping weights is uneconomic, and GPSR product-safety rules apply. Only a fake-door ad test fits the budget, and it needs care under ASA/consumer law.
scores.M_why: Rucking is a growing UK niche, but GoRuck and Amazon clones dominate. The feminine-branding angle is a slim differentiator, and trend risk is high [E].
scores.one_line: Physical, heavy, capital-hungry goods in a faddish niche: a poor fit for £300 and an agent-run model.

acquisition.why: SEO for '[industry] email lists' plus cold email to limited companies is legal and agent-runnable. The source's grey-hat SEO is fragile.

delivery.why: Scraping, enrichment and verification pipelines (Companies House API, verification APIs) are largely automatable. Accuracy sampling needs checks.

support.why: Bounce and refund disputes need judgement.

scores.R_why: The skills match well, and a Companies House-derived limited-company list is lawful. However, UK GDPR requires transparency notices to data subjects, plus legitimate-interest assessments. Selling sole-trader or consumer data, or enabling PECR-breaching outreach, risks ICO fines. Bought US consumer databases are a non-starter in the UK. The first-hand $30-50K/month claim is US and promotional.
scores.M_why: Apollo, Cognism, ZoomInfo and the free Companies House feed commoditise B2B data, and AI enrichment tools such as Clay erode it further. A defensible edge would need niche UK freshness, such as new-incorporation feeds [E].
scores.one_line: Highly automatable, but UK data-protection exposure and commoditised B2B data limit it to a narrow, lawful Companies House niche.

acquisition.why: Geo-targeted Meta/Google ads and local SEO are inbound, and walk-ins come from road frontage. The ads can be run by agents, but the reach is very local.

onboarding.why: Booking software, membership signup and smart-lock access are unattended.

delivery.why: Physical premises need cleaning, equipment maintenance and incident response, though access is self-serve.

billing.why: Recurring Stripe memberships through the booking software.

support.why: Lockouts, simulator faults and damage need a nearby human.

scores.R_why: It needs about £30-80K capital [E], a commercial lease, planning/change-of-use and insurance. Bromley/London rents are high. That is far beyond £300 and a part-time parent's risk tolerance. The evidence is unusually first-hand, but it is US-based.
scores.M_why: UK demand for golf simulators in winter is real and private single-bay concepts are under-supplied locally, but franchises are expanding [E].
scores.one_line: A well-evidenced, largely self-serve model, but the capital, lease and physical upkeep make it unrealistic for Ricardo's budget.

acquisition.why: Beehiiv newsletter growth is inbound, through SEO, referrals and recommendation networks, and agents can draft content. Voice and expertise need Ricardo's approval.

onboarding.why: Consulting engagements need discovery calls and scoping.

delivery.why: The consultant delivers personally, which consumes Ricardo's scarce hours.

scores.R_why: This is feasible in the UK if Ricardo has sellable technical expertise, such as AI automation. But consulting is a trade of hours, which contradicts the agent-run goal and 6-8 h/week. The claim is pure hypothetical maths, and growing to 2,000 subscribers takes many months.
scores.M_why: Niche B2B newsletters still work, but AI-written newsletters flood inboxes. Expertise and a distinct voice are the moat [E].
scores.one_line: Cheap to start and inbound-led, but delivery is Ricardo's own time, so it is a job rather than an agent-run business.
